units: pixels and seconds; image coords x right, y down, origin top-left

camera.motion: static (background gradient pixel values identical across frames; no features move)
camera.background: featureless underwater blue gradient; no ground plane, horizon or vanishing points
camera.view: camera looks up at the whale from below / side (belly-ish view, head at upper left)

objects.name: whale
objects.description: single dark-blue humpback-like whale (long pectoral fins), the only object; head upper-left, tail fluke lower-right in frames 0-50, tail swings up to the right by frame 71
objects.reference_point: ref_x/ref_y = 2D mask centroid (proxy for rig origin, which is not visible); head_x/head_y = centre of a template-tracked head/front-body patch (more rigid, better for scale)
objects.apparent_size_change: head template scale vs frame 0: 1.00 (f0) -> ~0.96 (f20) -> ~0.93 (f36) -> ~0.90 (f55) -> 0.88 (f71); whale recedes from the camera (depth grows ~13% if scale ~ 1/depth)

events.what: whale already swimming; frames 0 and 1 are identical (motion starts at frame 1->2)
tail fluke starts to be clipped by bottom image edge
last frame with tail clipped; tail fully visible again from frame 39
mask centroid y reaches max (~849) then turns upward (tail downstroke ends)
centroid x briefly stalls (~1399, frames 26-31) while tail strokes
tail lifts above the body line; bbox bottom stops moving up (~918) - fin now lowest point
